reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes paid OneCoin package tiers by linking prices to token allocations, coin conversion, and projected euro values. It applies time pressure by claiming that delaying a purchase reduces the coins received, forecasts substantially higher future coin prices, and offers token rewards for inviting another person. The records do not establish completed transactions, realized returns, or the accuracy of the stated projections, and the ASR may contain transcription errors.

opening.argument: The presentation uses conditional and approximate language rather than presenting returns as certain. It describes projected currency values at several hypothetical price points, explicitly calls one figure an “approximate value,” and says the future price “probably” could reach a range. That framing supports financial commentary or scenario analysis: viewers are shown how outcomes would vary if assumptions changed, not promised a fixed payout. The numerical examples therefore illustrate possible outcomes and timing sensitivity, while leaving the actual value dependent on future conditions.

this coin is going to be between 50 and 100 euros in your next two to three years and probably, even 150 euros per coin

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited package price and conversion language establish that scenarios are being discussed, but not that the speaker guarantees realization. The future-price statement includes “probably,” and the examples repeatedly use conditional “if” phrasing. The referral statement also does not establish that anyone was promised a return; it merely describes a possible way to obtain tokens.

probably, even 150 euros per coin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling figures approximate or conditional does not neutralize the presentation's persuasive forecast. The speaker still ties paid packages to specific coin quantities and then projects large euro values, including a stated future range. The surrounding language urges a quick decision, so the caveats function as presentation qualifiers rather than a meaningful warning about loss or nonperformance.

opening.argument: The video's stated subject is explaining participation and financial education, and its structure is demonstrative. The speaker says the packages include education about cryptocurrency, gold, and finance, then walks through a ProTrader example, difficulty numbers, token conversion, and sample calculations. The title likewise identifies packages and benefits rather than a personal solicitation. On this record, the central activity is an instructional walkthrough of how the system is represented as operating, which fits an educational or operational demonstration.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of calculations does not make the subject merely educational. The walkthrough is specifically organized around paid package levels, token quantities, coin conversion, and changing projected value. Explaining those mechanics can itself be the way a package is promoted, especially when the presentation emphasizes acting quickly.

the longer I delay to buy a package, the less coins I'm going to get
This is the opportunity

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational label is not supported by neutral instruction alone. The speaker does not simply explain cryptocurrency generally; the examples repeatedly calculate what buyers of named packages could receive and what those coins could be worth. The call to decide quickly makes the demonstration commercially persuasive, so the tutorial format does not remove its promotional function.

opening.argument: The observable offer can be understood as ordinary purchase of tiered educational products with associated package benefits. The slides present distinct package names, prices, token allocations, and split counts, while the narration explains how the example is calculated. That is a product-and-pricing presentation, not evidence of credential theft, a deposit request, or a completed transaction. The referral language mentions receiving tokens, but the supplied material does not show a downline, enrollment form, or guaranteed income mechanism. The record therefore supports ordinary commerce or service promotion without establishing scam conduct.

citations.quote: All the educational packages from the smallest startup forward
you can also get tokens when you invite another person to be part of the huamco community

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a credential request or completed transaction is not decisive when the presentation itself describes buying packages, mining tokens into coins, and future euro values. The displayed tiers are not merely ordinary course prices: they are linked to token multiplication, conversion, and appreciation. Referral tokens also remain a recruitment-linked benefit even without a shown enrollment form.

each of the packages has tokens from 1000 tokens 50000 10000 to 300,000 tokens

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The package tables and prices are evidence of more than ordinary educational-service commerce because the promised benefits are tied to token creation, coin conversion, and escalating projected values. The absence of a completed transaction does not change what the video invites viewers to buy. Likewise, the referral statement is additional evidence of participant recruitment, not proof that the offer is a conventional retail service.
